h: Torah Engraved in the Heart Makes Spiritual Growth Endure

p: שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת טו, כה)
"'There He made for them a statute and an ordinance, etc.' (Shemos 15:25):
because it is a rational mitzvah.
And so we find (in Bereishis Rabbah 65:16):
and I did not serve him
of how Esav served his father."
what a certain gentile did for his father
And certainly they did not come
that it is forbidden to say,
But this is not their praise;
who brought him into this world,
and all its desires and delights
Therefore even the nations accepted it,
and so it is in the Gemara, Kiddushin there):
"'All the kings of the earth shall acknowledge You, Hashem,
כִּי שָׁמְעוּ אִמְרֵי פִיךָ (תְּהִלִּים קלח, ד)
for they have heard the words of Your mouth' (Tehillim 138:4):
for it is a rational mitzvah
to which even the nations agree.
אַךְ לָמָּה דָּרְשׁוּ חֹק עַל שַׁבָּת
But why did they expound "statute" as Shabbos?
This is according to what is written
in Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah, Vayikra Rabbah 35:4):
"A human being issues a decree, etc.,
and has it fulfilled by others;
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵן
but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so:
I engraved heaven and earth, etc."
to walk in His ways and conduct,
and they are the sum of the words of Torah
with which He created His world;
And although they expounded in the Gemara (Berachos 6a):
"From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He,
"From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He,
but regarding Shabbos it is written explicitly (Shemos 20:11):
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
"For in six days Hashem made, etc.,
and He rested on the seventh day;
He commanded to walk in His ways;
and therefore Shabbos is called simply a "statute."
And this is what is expounded in the Mechilta:
ordinance — this is honoring father and mother."
"And they went three days in the wilderness
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב ס, עַמּוּד א)
the Torah had not been given to them!
that the Holy One, blessed be He,
the Holy One, blessed be He, etc."
That is, after they had had
for it says (in the Mechilta and the holy Zohar, Beshalach):
and afterward there was hidden from them
and this is "and they went three days"
And when he came to Marah,
he taught them statute and ordinance;
their keeping the statutes and ordinances
of the Holy One, blessed be He,
with which He created His world
as stated in the Midrash (beginning of Bereishis Rabbah):
I was the instrument of the craft
of the Holy One, blessed be He, etc."
only for the sake of Heaven,
because of the command of Hashem;
and this brings holiness into him,
as we bless for every mitzvah,
for in every mitzvah one attains holiness.
the sound of his mother's footsteps,
before the Shechinah that is coming";
that is, because of the mitzvah
"who dwells in the midst of the Children of Yisrael";
And about this it is said (Devarim 5:16):
to fulfill it because of the command of Hashem.
And this is what the verse says (Tehillim 147:19–20):
His statutes and ordinances to Yisrael;
He has not done so for any nation,
and ordinances they have not known, etc.";
from both the statutes and the ordinances,
And the entire Torah is counsel
on how to come to the recognition
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פב, עַמּוּד ב)
the Torah gives a person, etc."
Which is not so with the nations
they do not bring into them
of the light of Hashem and the utterance "I am";
which is not so with Yisrael,
from both the statutes and the ordinances.

p: And Rashi explains from Toras Kohanim:
that is, in the Torah she'b'al peh,
they said "we will do and we will hear,"
because there is not in it
and the holding of the mountain over them like a barrel
was about the Torah she'b'al peh,
for there is great pain in it
that it is engraved in the heart.
"For in much wisdom is much vexation"
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קיג, עַמּוּד א)
And so it is written in the holy Zohar (III 113a):
this is the Torah she'b'al peh, etc."
For through toil in words of Torah
the words of Torah are engraved in the heart;
For a person, all the days of his life,
כִּי הוֹלֵךְ הָאָדָם אֶל בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ
"For man goes to his eternal home."
"And I will give you places to walk
and a person, as long as he lives,
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
"I can no longer go out and come in";
for since he could no longer
he no longer had any business
And how can a person be sure
that he will be a walker,
And it says in the Gemara (Kiddushin 30b):
I created Torah as its antidote";
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this is through the Torah she'b'al peh
drag him to the beis midrash";
novel insights in the Torah she'b'al peh.
And then you will be secure:
that you will be able to be walkers
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ (וַיִּקְרָא כו, יא)
And this is what it says afterward (Vayikra 26:11):
"And I will place My Mishkan among you,
and My soul shall not reject you";
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, asked:
what kind of promise is this,
that He will not despise them?
And on the contrary, in the opposite case
But here it is a promise
that they will no longer be corrupted,
and the yetzer hara will not overpower you
so that you would, Heaven forbid,
from the turmoil of the yetzer hara.
"And I will establish My covenant with you";
and Rashi explains from Toras Kohanim:
that will not be broken, etc."
And Shabbos too is called a "statute,"
as stated in the Mechilta cited above:
That is, on Shabbos one merits
that it be engraved in the heart
for it says in the Yerushalmi
only for eating and drinking, etc.;
only for occupying oneself with words of Torah";
and it says in the Pesikta
the one who says "for Torah study"
And regarding talmidei chachamim we find (Shabbos 119a):
so that they would get up;
would go around to the pairs of Rabbis;
who are occupied with labor on weekdays,
that it be engraved in the heart.
And this is "if you walk in My statutes":
that the words of Torah be engraved
when their soul was bitter within them
over the departure of the illumination
they had had at the Sea,
for through Shabbos they would be secure
that it would be engraved in the heart
and they would no longer be corrupted;
"who keeps Shabbos from desecrating it, etc.":
(and in Pri Etz Chaim the wording is:
from the accusation of the yetzer hara).
And this is what we say on Motzaei Shabbos Kodesh,
with the knowledge of Your Torah";
and this is the Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א)
as Rashi explains (Parshas Ki Sisa, Shemos 31:3):
and it is "a spirit from the holiness above,"
as stated in the holy Zohar.
this is the Torah she'b'al peh."
And this is "the knowledge of Your Torah";
"and You have taught us to do the statutes of Your will"
for the words of Torah are engraved in the heart;
and through this they are secure
from the accusation of the yetzer hara in the future.

paragraphs.text: Source: Yeshayahu 56:2 — “אשרי אנוש יעשה זאת ובן אדם יחזיק בה שמר שבת מחללו ושמר ידו מעשות כל רע” — “Happy is the mortal who does this, The one who holds fast to it: Who keeps the sabbath and does not profane it, And holds back from doing any evil.”

— “Happy is the mortal who does this, The one who holds fast to it: Who keeps the sabbath and does not profane it, And holds back from doing any evil.”
